top.line: Two apps about what an agent can reach
top.para: José Bota's Hack the Agent teaches prompt injection in five levels; ReachCheck compares an agent's configuration with its mandate in the browser; both well made in a day, with a day's gaps and one shared next step.

in-short.para: Two apps; the game; its lesson; the checker; honesty; the gaps; a behaviour policy next.

apps.para: Built at the Vibathon about what an agent can reach; used with invented input, three live requests, the temporary session deleted.

arena.para: Five levels from a system prompt to a hardened agent, traces of allowed and blocked tool calls, a host dashboard with budgets, held up live; next: host recovery, nickname filtering, a session report, a policy card, name the model.

reachcheck.para: Import, mandate, review, export, entirely in the browser and honest about its limits; good on its demos, cautious to a fault on an invented support agent; next: possible matches from names and hints, wider injection checks, sharing, a policy, GitHub Pages.

together.para: A teaching tool and a review tool for one problem, both pointing to behaviour policies enforced outside the model.

limits.para: Two apps built in a day, used on 31 October; invented input; servers not tested in depth; inference about the server; my interest.

sources.para: My message of 31 October and our sessions with both apps.
